@graph.articleBody: You are on a ladder, under a sink or behind the wheel when the phone buzzes. A stranger wants a quote. You tell yourself you will answer later, and later turns into tonight. By then that person may have written to other businesses. That gap between the inquiry and the first answer is what marketers call speed to lead. Most of what you will find about it online is written for software companies with sales teams. This guide is written for a local service business where the owner is often the whole team. It covers what counts as a first reply, which channels to watch, how to cover them while you work, and what a good first message says. You will not find a magic response-time number here. itemListElement.name: Speed to Lead: Why the First Reply Matters for a Local Service Business

acceptedAnswer.text: Speed to lead is how quickly a real person answers a new inquiry from a potential customer. For a local service business, the inquiry can be a call, a form, a text, a WhatsApp message or a message on a social or Google profile.

mainEntity.name: How fast should I respond to a new lead?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no verified number to give you. The practical standard is to reply as soon as a real person can, and to make sure the customer is never left with nothing. If you cannot answer right away, an acknowledgment that a person will follow up is better than silence.

mainEntity.name: Does an automatic reply count as responding?

acceptedAnswer.text: It helps, but it is not a replacement. An automatic message confirms that the inquiry arrived, and a person still needs to follow up with the details the customer asked for.

mainEntity.name: Can not answering affect my Google Ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: For Local Services Ads, it can. Google says that if you regularly fail to answer calls or respond to messages, your ad ranking may be affected.
